name: @projexlight/hdk-image-editor
summary: On-device image editor for ProjexCloud's HDK (Hardware Development Kit) — JS bindings for native crop / rotate / annotate / mask / redact operations on iOS, Android, and desktop Electron. PII redaction (face detection + blur) runs locally so bystander images never leave the device. Output blobs get registered into sdk-evidence with the derivation chain intact.

endpoints.description: Returns supported ops (crop / rotate / annotate / mask / redact-faces / redact-text) per platform. Used by clients to feature-detect before invoking native bindings.

events.name: hdk.image-editor.applied.v1
events.description: An editing op was applied to a source image. Carries op_kind + source_evidence_id + derived_evidence_id for the chain-of-custody trail.

events.name: hdk.image-editor.redaction-fired.v1
events.description: PII redaction op fired (face / text / license-plate). Carries detector model + count_redacted.

events.name: hdk.image-editor.capability-probed.v1
events.description: Client probed capabilities; useful for adoption telemetry.

hooks.name: applyOp
hooks.description: Universal entry — { source_blob, op_kind, params } → { derived_blob, derivation_metadata }. Op happens on-device via native binding.

hooks.name: redactFaces
hooks.description: Convenience wrapper around applyOp({ op_kind: 'redact-faces' }) using the on-device face-detection model.

hooks.name: redactText
hooks.description: OCR + blur for license plates, ID numbers, badges. Tenant policy can require this on capture for certain workflows.

hooks.name: registerDerivation
hooks.description: After an op, register the derived blob as a sdk-evidence variant; preserves the derivation chain end-to-end.

ui_components.name: ImageEditorCanvas
ui_components.description: Native-rendered canvas with op palette; consumes applyOp + redactFaces. Themed via @projexlight/design-system.

scenarios.title: Insurance claim photo: redact bystander faces on-device
scenarios.when_to_use: Claim photo includes bystanders not party to the claim; redact before the image leaves the device so it never lands on a remote server with unredacted PII.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Derived blob with faces blurred. Emits hdk.image-editor.applied.v1 + .redaction-fired.v1. sdk-evidence holds the variant linked to the source — adjudication can replay the original-vs-redacted comparison.

scenarios.title: Field tech captures a vehicle photo; license plate auto-stripped
scenarios.when_to_use: Field-service / fleet tenants whose policy disallows storing plates. Capture-time op runs before the photo enters the evidence chain.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Plate region blurred. Tenant policy violation refused (return error to the UI) if the user tries to skip redaction on a flow where it's required.

scenarios.title: Adjuster annotates a damage photo with arrows + circles
scenarios.when_to_use: Pre-decision adjudication: senior reviewer marks specific damage areas before assigning a claim band.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns annotated derived blob. Annotation flattened into the image so the trail can't be edited later. Audit chain shows actor.persona + the shape params.

scenarios.title: User uploads a sideways scan; auto-rotate + crop to content
scenarios.when_to_use: Document-heavy flows where camera orientation produces awkward source files. Rotate + crop on-device before upload to save bandwidth + storage.
scenarios.example_code:
import { applyOp } from '@projexlight/hdk-image-editor';
const clean = await applyOp({ source_blob_id, op_kind: 'auto-rotate-crop' });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the rotated + cropped blob. Source preserved; the rotation/crop is reversible via the derivation metadata for legal review.

scenarios.title: Client checks capabilities before offering an op in the UI
scenarios.when_to_use: Cross-platform UI: not every device supports every op (e.g. license-plate OCR may be desktop-only). UI calls the capabilities endpoint to feature-detect.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the ops array. Tenant-wide feature-flagging via sdk-feature-flags can further restrict which ops are surfaced in the UI.

compliance_posture.notes: On-device redaction is the GDPR Art-25 + HIPAA de-identification lever — un-redacted images never leave the device for workflows that require it. Face-detector model is local; no biometric template is persisted (BIPA-friendly). Capability probe + applied events satisfy AI Act per-op logging.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per op applied on a source (rotate / crop / annotate / redact)
per redaction op (free in healthcare / finserv packs)
